extra_misconceptions.fact: Offset lithography uses a flat planographic plate that transfers ink to a rubber blanket cylinder before pressing onto the paper.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Offset lithography uses raised metal letters on the plate cylinder to press ink directly onto the moving paper web.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Gravure cylinders hold liquid ink inside etched recessed cells while a steel doctor blade wipes the raised surface clean.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Gravure printing holds ink on the raised surface areas of the cylinder while the recessed cells remain completely dry.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Digital presses image each sheet directly from computer data using laser drums or inkjet heads without physical printing plates.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Digital laser printers require a new aluminum or photopolymer printing plate whenever a single word changes on the page.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Screen printing pushes heavy ink layers through mesh stencils onto curved glass bottles, circuit boards, metal signs, and textiles.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Screen printing works only on flat cotton T-shirts and cannot deposit thick opaque ink onto glass, metal, or plastic.

extra_socratic_questions: What physical principle keeps ink and fountain solution separate on a flat offset lithography printing plate?
Which microscopic ink-edge pattern under a loupe distinguishes a gravure sample from a relief-printed sample?
Under what run-length and variable-data conditions does digital printing cost less per sheet than offset?
What happens to the printed image orientation if an offset plate transfers ink directly to paper without a blanket?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Halftone screens simulate shades of gray by printing tiny solid black dots of varying sizes spaced across white paper.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Halftone printing creates gray shades by mixing black ink with white ink in different ratios inside the press fountain.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scaling up a low-resolution raster image stretches existing pixels over a larger area, producing blurry or jagged edges in print.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Enlarging a 72-PPI web graphic to twelve inches wide in page layout software automatically adds sharp print detail.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Vector graphics store shapes as mathematical paths and curves that scale to any dimension without losing edge sharpness.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Vector illustrations store images as a fixed grid of colored pixels that lose clarity whenever the art is resized.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Commercial presses print with subtractive CMYK inks, which have a smaller color gamut than additive RGB computer monitors.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: RGB color files sent directly to a four-color commercial press will match the bright neon colors seen on a monitor.

extra_socratic_questions: Why can a standard offset press not print a continuous-tone photograph without first converting it into a halftone screen?
What happens to the sharpness of a raster bitmap logo compared to a vector file when scaled up to poster size?
What measurement in lines per inch or dots per inch confirms that a scanned image has enough resolution for print?
Under what condition does saving line art as a heavily compressed JPEG introduce visible blocky artifacts around sharp edges?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Limiting a layout to one or two contrasting typefaces establishes clear visual hierarchy and keeps body copy legible.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Combining four or five fancy script typefaces on one poster makes the event announcement easier to read from afar.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Background graphics must extend at least one-eighth inch past the trim edge as bleed to prevent white paper gaps.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Stopping a full-color background box right on the exact page edge guarantees ink will reach the border after trimming.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Deliberate white space separates information groups, reduces visual clutter, and guides the reader toward key messages.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Filling every square inch of a flyer with text and clip art maximizes visual impact and reader comprehension.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Print shops require packaged font files, high-resolution linked graphics, or a press-ready PDF with embedded fonts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sending a native layout document to a print shop without fonts or linked images ensures the text prints identically.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to reader eye flow and visual hierarchy when five decorative display fonts compete on a single flyer?
Where should background artwork extend relative to the trim line so no unprinted white slivers appear after cutting?
Which physical indicator on a proof reveals that body copy leading is set too tight for comfortable reading?
What measurement confirms that critical text sits safely inside the margin away from the guillotine cutter path?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Plastisol ink requires heat curing at roughly 320 degrees Fahrenheit so the PVC resin fuses into the fabric fibers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Plastisol screen-printing ink air-dries permanently on cotton shirts within ten minutes of sitting on a drying rack.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Excess water emulsifies the offset ink, causing washed-out gray solids, snowflaking, and slow drying on the delivery pile.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Adding excess fountain solution to an offset press makes the printed ink look darker and dry faster on coated stock.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Open mesh areas between the stencil and the frame must be taped off so stray ink does not squeeze onto the garment.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Leaving screen mesh edges unmasked around a small stencil saves tape without affecting the clean margins of the shirt.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pressroom solvents and stencil strippers release fumes and irritate skin, requiring nitrile gloves, goggles, and ventilation.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Washout solvents and press blanket cleaners are harmless household soaps that need neither gloves nor shop ventilation.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a photo-emulsion screen stencil if it is exposed to sunlight before the washout step is finished?
Why is it dangerous to reach toward a moving offset cylinder or belt to clear a jammed sheet while the press runs?
Which physical indicator on a test print shows that squeegee angle or flood pressure changed mid-stroke?
What measurement or registration mark check confirms that the image sits square on all 50 sheets during the press run?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Commercial binderies use hollow rotating steel bits on a paper drill press to bore clean holes through thick paper lifts.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Print shops punch binder holes into a 500-sheet stack of paper using a standard desktop three-hole squeeze punch.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Thick nested signatures cause inner pages to extend past outer pages, making perfect binding better for thick publications.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Saddle stitching can bind a 400-page catalog cleanly without the center folded signatures pushing outward at the fore-edge.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Perfect binding glues page edges into a flat spine that resists lying flat, whereas spiral coils let pages fold all the way back.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Perfect-bound paperback books open completely flat to 360 degrees just like spiral-bound notebooks on a music stand.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Padding adhesive is painted onto only one clamped edge backed by chipboard so individual sheets tear off cleanly.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Padding compound must be brushed heavily across all four sides of a notepad stack so the sheets stay together.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to bypass the two-hand safety switches on a powered guillotine paper cutter during trimming?
What happens to the outer edges of a thick saddle-stitched booklet before a face trim removes page creep?
Under what page-count and usage condition is perfect binding or case binding chosen instead of saddle stitching?
Which physical indicator on the spine distinguishes a sewn hardcover case binding from a glued paperback perfect bind?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Newspaper plants unwind continuous rolls of newsprint through high-speed web offset presses that print, fold, and trim inline.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Daily newspapers feed individual cut sheets of paper one at a time through small tabletop printers for morning delivery.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Commercial plants inspect press sheets inside standardized 5000-Kelvin viewing booths and measure color bars with densitometers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Press operators judge color accuracy under whatever fluorescent shop bulbs happen to hang above the delivery tray.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Every commercial print job travels with a detailed job jacket or digital ticket specifying stock, ink, quantity, and finishing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Verbal instructions passed between shifts are sufficient to run a complex multi-color job without a written job ticket.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Printing plants bale paper waste and recycle used aluminum plates to recover material costs and reduce environmental waste.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Aluminum offset plates and paper trimmings from a newspaper press run must be thrown into general landfill dumpsters.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a print job deadline if the prepress department skips customer proofing before burning metal plates?
Where should visitors stand and what personal protective gear must they wear near high-speed web presses and folders?
Which physical indicator on a press sheet color bar tells the operator that cyan ink density has drifted off target?
What measurement on a job ticket tracks a project as it moves from estimation through prepress, press, and bindery?

extra_misconceptions.fact: The graphic communications industry includes prepress specialists, color scientists, packaging engineers, estimators, and press operators.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Graphic arts careers are limited strictly to freelance logo designers working alone on laptops at coffee shops.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Designers who understand press registration, bleed, folding, and paper weight avoid costly production errors and reprints.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Graphic designers only need artistic talent and never need to understand paper grain, ink trapping, or bindery limits.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Automated presses require trained technicians who can calibrate spectrophotometers, troubleshoot workflows, and maintain machinery.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Automation and computer-to-plate systems have eliminated the need for skilled human technicians in modern printing plants.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many graphic arts professionals enter through trade schools, community college certificates, union apprenticeships, or print programs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A four-year fine art painting degree is the only educational path accepted for technical roles in commercial printing.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a designer's artwork on press when a prepress technician finds missing bleeds or low-resolution images?
Which portfolio artifacts demonstrate that a graphic arts applicant understands production constraints as well as design?
Under what condition must a packaging designer collaborate directly with a structural die-cutter and press operator?
What measurement and color-management skills distinguish a trained press operator from an entry-level bindery helper?
